@graph.comment: ViewAssembler (view-layer spec §3.1) — executes the view descriptors' declared CONSTRUCT/SELECT projection queries via embedded @comunica/query-sparql over EXPLICIT sources (no link traversal; the Pod hosts no SPARQL endpoint per D3/D29). Parameterless: engine + serializers are constructed internally. Shared by both view HTTP handlers.

ViewHttpHandler — per-resource ?_profile= conneg (view-layer spec §4): doc|fused|graph|alt over /vault/wiki/* resources. Inserted BEFORE LdpHandler in the BaseHttpHandler waterfall (same QSA-interception precedent as WikiSearchHttpHandler / MementoHttpHandler), so ?_profile-shaped GETs are claimed before standard LDP processing and fall through (NotImplementedHttpError) otherwise. store = urn:solid-server:default:ResourceStore = the MonitoringStore instance (the Monitoring-level store): internal reads MUST NOT pass through the TrailerDecoratingStore, which sits ABOVE Monitoring and only decorates the outbound LDP read path. baseUrl is the deployment baseUrl variable (NOT a literal); viewsBase is the pod-specific view-descriptor container (hardcoded string, same idiom as the AdmissionFloor stampPredicate / markdown-render storagePath).

ViewSpaceHttpHandler — the /vault/views/ cross-cutting virtual URL space (view-layer spec §6; Person demonstrator at /vault/views/people/). Read-only; assembles one entity from its multiple writable homes via a descriptor CONSTRUCT, sources enumerated through the Type Index (no source hardcode, D107). Inserted BEFORE LdpHandler alongside ViewHttpHandler. Same Monitoring-level store ref as ViewHttpHandler (bypasses the trailer). viewSpaceRoot = the served container path; typeIndexUrl = the Type Index used to enumerate person-class source containers.

TrailerDecoratingStore (view-layer spec §4.3, decision A′) — the conditional dynamic trailer on default GET. A PassthroughStore that decorates ONLY the outbound LDP read path: it wraps urn:solid-server:default:ResourceStore (the MonitoringStore) and is referenced by the LDP OperationHandler (below) so it sits ABOVE Monitoring in the read path. Internal consumers (markdown-projection / mem-trigger / ops-index listeners, the two view handlers) all reference urn:solid-server:default:ResourceStore directly and therefore BYPASS the trailer — internal reads never see it. Note we do NOT re-@id the MonitoringStore as the trailer: ResourceStore must stay a MonitoringStore so its `changed` event subscription (CDC) keeps working — a PassthroughStore at that @id would emit no events. auxiliaryStrategy is the standard CSS strategy (used to skip decorating .meta auxiliaries).

Interpose the TrailerDecoratingStore ABOVE MonitoringStore on the LDP read path. The LDP OperationHandler (config/ldp/handler/components/operation-handler.json) is a StatusWaterfallHandler whose Get/Post/Put/Delete/Head/Patch handlers all reference urn:solid-server:default:ResourceStore (= Monitoring) inline. We replace the whole handlers list (overrideParameters — the handlers are anonymous inline objects with no @id to anchor an InsertBefore against) so every operation handler reads/writes through urn:cogitarelink:ResourceStore_Trailer instead. The trailer is a plain passthrough for writes (events still fire once at Monitoring below it) and only decorates GET responses that carry mem:hasOpenAction. The StaticThrowHandler (405 MethodNotAllowed fallback) is replicated verbatim at the tail. CAVEAT (same tradeoff as the K1 overrideParameters workaround): this snapshots the upstream OperationHandler shape, so a CSS bump that adds an operation handler must be mirrored here.
